chapter: Broadway, tenors, Billie Holiday and Rhythm Club memories
title: Coleman Hawkins's decline

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Did you see Hawk very often during the last years....

No I didn't. I didn't see Hawk all the time that he was growing a beard. I didn't see the Hawk. I know that one time we were all by to see Shorty Baker, he was at the Alvin Hotel and we all stopped by to see him, he wasn't feeling too well.
No, Horace Silver, not Horace Silver.

No. A trumpet player. Anyway he came by, he says 'Hot doggit, it you know who I just saw? Hawk out there on Broadway, looked just like Jesus.' Well I hadn't seen Hawk. See, and then, Evelyn hadn't seen Hawk really perform, see, because I been knowing Hawk way back there before I even started, you see I knew Hawk way before he knew me. And Hawk always used to dress immaculate and keep that horn immaculate, man, just as clean, at the time. There was a store there, Laytons and Phil Kronfield, where you used to go buy men's clothes, Hawk used to go there then, way back there then to buy hundred-dollar suits, two hundred-dollar suits, tuxedos, man, he was a beautiful dresser. So he came here to Columbus and I wrote to Evelyn and said, please go by and see Coleman Hawkins because he's a great tenor player, which he was, and she went by and she says, 'Cozy, I know that you may not like this but he just looked terrible. He had this beard, it wasn't combed, his suit wasn't pressed, like cigarette ashes all over his tuxedo, and they had to help him up on the bandstand, and he said it was just terrible.'
Well he was drinking himself to death.
Yep, and said he could hardly play. I said oh, that's too bad. So that was her thoughts of Coleman Hawkins, the only time she heard him. But see I knew better

than that at the time that Hawk was well, you know, but he just drank himself to death. Drank himself to death, it was too bad. I don't know for what reason. You never know what's on anybody's mind that does something like that. They say he just went down to nothing. And with that beard growing, he wouldn't comb it (TOO LOW) ... Roy Eldridge told me about him. He said 'Cozy, you wouldn't want to see Hawk, knowing Hawk in the earlier years.' He was a fashion plate.
Oh yeah, he had expensive tastes and everything.
Oh boy, all the tenor players loved him. All the tenor players used to almost cry when they'd hear Hawk play the last year or so that they were out there. Because he wasn't playing anything.
